page.h1: HTS Chapter 38: Miscellaneous Chemical Products — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Tariffs on U.S. Chemical Products by Country (HTS Ch. 38) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What the EU, Canada, Mexico, China, Japan, Brazil, South Korea and Singapore charge on U.S. pesticides, reagents, catalysts and other Chapter 38 goods, and which regulator approves them.

intro: Tariffs are zero for most of this chapter's trade: Canada, Mexico and South Korea charge nothing on qualifying U.S. goods, Singapore charges nothing at all, and the EU has charged nothing since July 1, 2026 (except 3809.10 and 3824.60). China adds a 10% extra duty to MFN rates of up to 13%, Brazil charges the Mercosur tariff of up to 14%, and Japan up to 3.9%. For most Chapter 38 goods the real gate is product approval in the buyer's market: pesticide and biocide registration (PMRA in Canada, MAPA in Brazil, the EU's plant-protection and biocides rules), diagnostic-device approval for reagents (3822), and chemical registration such as REACH, K-REACH and China's new-substance rules. Each market's regulator is listed below.

profile.headline: The EU is the largest market ($8.32B, 23% of the chapter, up 1.5%), led by diagnostic and laboratory reagents (3822, $4.34B), most of which were already duty-free. Since July 1, 2026 Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 has also zeroed the EU's duties of up to 6.5% on U.S. chemical preparations, catalysts and fuel additives; registration under REACH, the biocides rules or the IVD Regulation still decides whether a product can be sold.
profile.mainProducts: Diagnostic & laboratory reagents (3822) · Other chemical preparations (n.e.s.) (3824)

regulator.name: European Chemicals Agency (REACH, biocides), Member State pesticide authorities and IVDR notified bodies
regulator.requirement: Substances in a preparation imported at 1 tonne a year or more must be registered under REACH; biocides need approval under Regulation (EU) 528/2012, plant protection products an EU-approved active substance plus a Member State authorisation (Regulation (EC) 1107/2009), and diagnostic reagents CE marking under Regulation (EU) 2017/746

profile.headline: Canada ($5.59B, down 2.7%) is the largest single buyer and takes 40% of U.S. pesticide exports (3808, $1.79B) and most U.S. biodiesel. Qualifying goods enter free and neither of Canada's counter-tariff lists has a Chapter 38 item; the gate is PMRA registration for any pest control product.
profile.mainProducts: Pesticides, herbicides & disinfectants (3808) · Other chemical preparations (n.e.s.) (3824)

regulator.name: Health Canada's Pest Management Regulatory Agency (PMRA), plus Health Canada device licensing and ECCC New Substances
regulator.requirement: A pest control product must be registered under the Pest Control Products Act before it is imported, sold or used; Class II–IV diagnostic devices need a medical device licence, and a chemical not on the Domestic Substances List must be notified before import

profile.headline: Mexico ($4.02B, down 8.1%) buys catalysts (3815, $0.97B) and chemical preparations (3824, $0.92B) for its refineries and plants. Qualifying goods enter free; Mexico's MFN rates on the national lines in the sample run 0%–15%, so a valid USMCA certification of origin matters.

regulator.name: COFEPRIS (pesticide registrations and import permits, diagnostic reagents)
regulator.requirement: Pesticides and disinfectants need a COFEPRIS registration and import permit, and diagnostic reagents are health supplies that need a COFEPRIS sanitary registration; confirm the permit with the importer of record

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: Singapore import requirements

assumptions: MFN rates are the World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) simple-average applied rates for one representative six-digit subheading per heading — the subheading with the largest 2025 U.S. exports in that heading (for example 3822.19 for diagnostic reagents, 3824.99 for other chemical preparations and 3808.93 for herbicides) — for 2023, the latest year WITS holds for these markets. National 8–10-digit lines can differ, and where a subheading has several national lines the basis gives their range.
For Mexico, Brazil and Singapore, WITS holds 2023 schedules only in HS 2017 codes, so 3822.19 uses HS 3822.00 and 3827.68 uses HS 3824.78 (the codes these goods were classified under before HS 2022).

USMCA (Mexico, Canada), KORUS (South Korea) and the U.S.–Singapore FTA give 0% to U.S. goods that meet the agreement's rules of origin; the normal-rate column shows each market's MFN rate for goods that do not qualify.

For the EU, Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 sets 0% on U.S.-origin goods of Chapter 38 except 3809.10 and 3824.60 from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029, on proof of non-preferential U.S. origin; the normal-rate column shows the rate the EU charged before then. The Commission can suspend the cut.

China's cells add the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods to its MFN rate. China's 2018–2019 counter-tariffs (answering the U.S. Section 301 tariffs) also still apply to listed lines — Annex 3 of the May 2019 notice alone lists 22 Chapter 38 lines at 10% — unless an exclusion has been granted; they are not added because exclusions are granted line by line.
Brazil and Japan show MFN rates. India, not in this table, charges a basic customs duty of 0%–10% on the same subheadings (WITS, 2023), before surcharges.
